industry.ipm: Indian domestic formulations market ₹2,565 bn in FY26, +9.9% (₹2,334 bn in FY25) (IQVIA, AR FY26 industry section)
industry.ipmGrowth: Q4FY26 IPM +10.7% ex-GLP-1 innovator (Mankind +8.7%); Q1FY27 IPM +13.0% ex-tirzepatide (Mankind +12.7%) (company decks)
industry.priceGrowth: FY26 price growth: Mankind 4.2%, industry 4.4% (IQVIA, Q4FY26 call); price increases on scheduled drugs are capped by the WPI-linked NLEM/DPCO mechanism, ~10% a year allowed on non-scheduled drugs
industry.glp1: Semaglutide's Indian patent expired in Mar-2026 and 20+ companies launched 35-40 brands (oral and injectable); prices fell sharply. Mankind launched a semaglutide pen (in-licensed) in Apr-May 2026 through two divisions (diabetes and gynaec) and is not chasing price; IPM growth figures quoted by Mankind exclude tirzepatide / GLP-1 innovator brands
industry.chronicShift: IPM is moving toward chronic and specialty therapies (cardiac, diabetes, respiratory, CNS, oncology); Mankind's chronic share (ex-BSV) rose from 28% (FY18) to 39% (FY26) and 40% (Q1FY27)
industry.consumer: OTC/consumer health is shifting to modern trade and e-commerce (15% of Mankind's consumer sales in Q1FY27 vs 9% in FY25); general trade is soft

strengths: Prescription leadership: #1 in prescriptions for nine years (15.2% share) with 84% prescriber penetration and 5 lakh+ doctors covered by 18,500+ reps
Brand building at mass scale: 22 brands above ₹100 cr; #2 by volume; low-price, high-volume acute franchises in Tier II-VI and rural India
Consumer brands with category leadership: Manforce condoms 28%, Prega News 84%, Unwanted-72 68%, Acnestar 34% (IQVIA retail MAT Jun-26)
BSV: the only recombinant Anti-D (India patent to 2028), biosimilar rFSH, HMG, immunoglobulins: hard-to-make biologics with few competitors
Cost discipline and in-house manufacturing; employee cost held near 22% of sales
weaknesses: 60% of domestic sales are acute, where Mankind has grown only in line with the market since FY25
Late and cautious in GLP-1s; new introductions 2.8% of sales vs 4.1% for the IPM (Q1FY27)
Chronic share (40%) well below chronic-led peers
Consumer healthcare has grown ~5% a year for two years
ROCE 12% after paying ~28x EBITDA for BSV

critiques: Growth gap: Mankind beat the IPM by 1.3-1.7x for years but grew below it in FY26 (organic domestic ex-OTC +8.6%) after an enforced field-force overhaul; JM Financial calls the acceleration 'elusive'
BSV disclosure: management stopped giving BSV revenue after integration and quoted only growth rates; analysts (Macquarie, Q3FY26 call) could not reconcile the numbers
'Cash EPS' adds back all D&A, not just acquisition amortisation
Income-tax search adjustments of ₹1,909 cr under appeal
Exports +29% in Q1 owed 12-13pp to the rupee
gaps: BSV's standalone revenue and EBITDA after Oct-2024 are not disclosed (only Q3FY26 revenue of ~₹464 cr and growth rates); BSV FY26 revenue is not known

The BSV purchase-price amortisation is not disclosed as a figure; we use ~₹450 cr a year from the Q1FY27 call (half of ~₹225 cr quarterly D&A), consistent with the FY24-25 step-up in intangible amortisation
Final purchase-price allocation: goodwill unchanged at ₹6,492.63 cr at Mar-26 (provisional ₹6,472.61 cr in FY25)
